claim_resolution.rationale: FirstLight's current data-center page identifies its active Brunswick facility and publishes present operating specifications. A MaineDOT utility record independently associates FirstLight with 14 Resilient Circle, matching the mapped building. Contemporaneous local reporting states that Resilient Tier-V had opened its doors at the former Brunswick Naval Air Station by September 28, 2011, supplying an operational-no-later-than event for the exact facility. The current 52,000-square-foot facility figure is accepted as an exact-facility observation; Oxford Networks is retained only as the historical seed name.

Element Critical's current Chicago page identifies Chicago Two at 341 Haynes Drive, matching the CH2 seed and mapped building, and offers active colocation, support, security, and tour services. Its 45,000-square-foot property size and 5 MW power value are exact-facility observations.

UF's construction record defines the East Campus building as a data center with a dedicated High Performance Computing Center. UFIT's maintained history identifies the East Campus facility as opened in 2012, HiPerGator production there from 2013, and later generations through the 2025 retirement of HiPerGator 2.0. The 2012 opening is retained as a year-precision operational event; together the first-party records establish the mapped East Campus research-computing facility and current operation. The 2011 area figure was prospective and is not normalized.

Sandia's 2019 facility map explicitly identifies the Building 880 Annex as a data center serving enterprise and HPC systems. Sandia's current HPC site independently places active HPC training and support activity in Building 880/A1N. The exact building number, operator, and HPC function match the seed; the combined first-party evidence supports continued operation, with lower confidence because the current page describes the training room rather than the annex equipment floor.

Markley's current facility page identifies its active Lowell data center, describes 24x7 staffing and operating infrastructure, and reports 352,000 square feet. Its current contact page maps the Lowell location to One Markley Way, matching the mapped building. Markley's November 23, 2015 operator post states that Phase One had opened and customers had begun occupying the Lowell facility, supplying a conservative operational-no-later-than event.

EdgeConneX's DET01 data sheet identifies the exact facility code and 21005 Lahser Road address and publishes active operating, security, compliance, space, and power specifications. The City of Southfield identifies that address as a vacant shell planned for conversion to a Tier III data center in its 2012-2013 financial report, while EdgeConneX's March 11, 2015 release describes its Southfield Edge Data Center in service-provider partnership terms. Together these records establish operation no later than March 11, 2015 without treating the earlier forecast as an opening date. The 39,900-square-foot facility size and 3 MW value are accepted as exact-facility observations.

CoreSite's current AT2 page identifies 1130 Powers Ferry Place and offers active facility services, staffing, security, and specifications. CoreSite's 2022 integration announcement independently ties that exact address to the former DataSite Atlanta facility. The current 67,000-square-foot facility figure is accepted; DataSite is retained as a historical seed label and CoreSite is the current operator record.

SAP's 2025 first-party list establishes that a Colorado Springs data center currently operates SAP cloud services, and a local building-department record documents a data-center project at 2345 Windswept View. A directory maps the COS02 code to that address and calls it operational, but the reviewed official and operator sources do not make the code-to-building link. Under the national policy, market-level operation plus an uncorroborated directory mapping cannot establish this exact building's lifecycle status.
